item.title: Alien Code
item.description: The idea behind the film boils down to one question: how would beings from a fourth spatial dimension see our world? It’s a great premise, and I loved it. Unfortunately, the execution is shaky. The script often feels like it was written by a child, and there are far too many moments that fall apart as soon as you think about them. The secret agents are cartoonish stereotypes. Then there is the scene where the protagonists “break into” a supposedly ultra-secret base. Seriously? No perimeter, no barbed-wire fence, no guards — they simply walk in through a white hatch on a hillside.

item.title: It's a Wonderful Life
item.description: A heartfelt, beautifully told story about a man who comes to see the quiet but profound value of his own life. I watched the colourised version.

item.title: The Usual Suspects
item.description: Excellent film with one of cinema’s most iconic twist endings.

item.title: Project Hail Mary
item.description:
I fell for the hype. This film clearly had an aggressive marketing campaign — every other outlet covered it, pitched as a faithful book adaptation, the best sci-fi in years, and so on. In reality it’s a simple story that would have made a great 30-minute short. Instead I sat through two-plus hours of it. That’s all I’ve got.

P.S. I genuinely don’t understand why this film has such a high rating.
